Member entity lifecycle today: `status` is written once at create (`inviteData.ts:289`, hardcoded `'active'`); no code path anywhere flips it afterward — #255 is greenfield for the write side.

## Sign-in failure-mode facts (done-when #6, "engineering's proposal")

- A tri-state `membership: 'loading'|'member'|'non-member'` already exists on both the agenda (`routes/+page.svelte`) and event-detail pages, driven by the status-scoped `findMyMemberId` (read #2). A deactivated member resolves to `'non-member'` with ZERO new code and gets a disabled RSVP control plus an explicit `rsvp_non_member_hint` i18n message ("Only members can RSVP") — this is NOT a blank/broken control, it already reads as a coherent, if terse, "you can't do this" state.
- The roster page itself is not membership-gated to view (any signed-in domain reader can open `/roster`, per its own header comment) — a deactivated member can still open it, she just won't see her own row.
- The agenda/events list is domain-wide, not membership-gated — she still sees the whole calendar.
- The gap: rights (`_owner`/`_editor`, reads #9/#10) are completely independent of `member.status`. If the deactivated person happened to hold an admin/librarian grant, deactivating her `member` entity leaves her a fully-powered admin — able to see/manage the very roster she's been removed from, and to deactivate/reactivate other members. This is the sharpest engineering decision the proposal needs to make explicit: either (a) deactivate also strips `_owner`/`_editor` as part of the same action, or (b) it deliberately does not, and an admin who leaves the choir must be separately demoted — but it must be a *stated* choice, not a silent gap.
- The other genuine regression: read #6 (season-summary) drops a deactivated member's entire attendance history from the conductor's view the moment she's deactivated, because that view's row set is the active roster, not the historical record. This directly tensions done-when #3's "past attendance... keep their subject" — the record itself stays intact in Entu (no data loss), but a conductor can no longer SEE it through this surface. Worth flagging even though it renders as "invisible", not "blank/id" as done-when #3 literally describes.

No implementation was done — this is the read-only fact-gathering pass the task specified.

verify.notes:
SCOPE: read-only investigation for #252 (arrange indent/unindent findability), sequenced deliberately AFTER #253 (the write-integrity bug). No files changed.

WHERE THE CONTROLS LIVE TODAY — src/routes/roster/+page.svelte
- Guards: canIndent (:1310) — prevSiblingId(id) !== null; canUnindent (:1319) — findSectionNode(...).parentId ?? null !== null (top-level parent is the org/db entity per #161, so nothing above it to promote to).
- Write seam: performReparent (:1360-1400) — reparentSection (moves _parent) then ONE reorderSections call over the destination sibling group (visibleSiblingsOf, post-optimistic-patch order); on throw: reorderError=true, refetch via listSections and reconcile, or fall back to the pre-write `before` snapshot if the refetch itself fails. handleIndent/handleUnindent (:1406/:1420) and the ArrowRight/ArrowLeft keyboard branch (handleHandleKeydown, calls at :2107/:2116) both funnel through this one seam.
- Guard flag: structuralWritePending = reorderPending || renamePending || removePending (:1490) — disables every indent/unindent/rename/delete button app-wide while any one structural write (reorder, reparent, rename, delete) is outstanding.
- Markup (:3049-3082): two <button type="button"> siblings of the row (not children — avoids nested-interactive inside the row's role="button"), data-testid="arrange-indent-{id}" / "arrange-unindent-{id}", aria-label + title via m.roster_section_indent/unindent, disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId===row.id || !canIndent/canUnindent(id)}, tabindex="-1" (deliberate, pointer/touch-only — keyboard equivalent is row-grab + Arrow keys), class="rounded p-1 text-ink-2 hover:text-ink disabled:cursor-default disabled:opacity-30", each holding one aria-hidden SVG viewBox="0 0 16 16" class="h-3 w-3 fill-current" with mirror-image triangle paths (indent: M4 2 L12 8 L4 14 Z / unindent: M12 2 L4 8 L12 14 Z). No text node in either button (accessible name comes solely from aria-label, by design, to keep textContent assertions like "Soprano (4)" clean).

WHAT #252 ASKS (Done-when, 7 items): (1) both controls meet the app's own min-h-11/min-w-11 touch standard; (2) only applicable actions render as tappable — inapplicable ones don't sit at opacity-30, but their space is reserved so rows don't jump; (3) the two directions read as distinguishable at a glance — engineering picks glyphs/label/icon treatment and states which+why; (4) color moves off the muted text-ink-2 to the app's normal control tone; (5) keyboard path (row-grab, Space/Enter, ArrowLeft/Right, tabindex="-1") is UNCHANGED — explicitly told not to "fix" tabindex="-1", it's pinned in page.roster-indent.spec.ts; (6) structuralWritePending keeps disabling everything mid-write; (7) nesting itself (recursive sections) is untouched — this is a findability fix only, not a feature removal.

Also carried in #252's own top comment (correction, dated same day): the issue no longer explains Joosep's "tagasi ei saa" report — that's now #253's half-landed-write banner. #252 stands as a real, independent tap-target/findability defect, but is explicitly sequenced to land AFTER #253 so a fixed write isn't made easier to trigger while still broken.

SPEC COVERAGE — src/routes/page.roster-indent.spec.ts (904 lines), all under #155/S3:
- :306 button presence, type, aria-label naming, "always visible / no grab needed"
- :326 enabled/disabled guard matrix (sop/sop1/sop2/alto/tenor across canIndent/canUnindent)
- :348-399 DOM containment: buttons are row SIBLINGS, no nested-interactive, no accessible-name leakage into the row's own label
- :401-461 indent → reparentSection + destination-group renumber, roll-up counts update
- :462-531 unindent → org-level and grandparent-level promotion targets
- :532-629 keyboard ArrowRight/ArrowLeft parity with the buttons, including refused-move-keeps-grab cases
- :631-717 shared reorderPending/structuralWritePending guard across reparent+renumber, and the failure-reconcile contract (console.error, listSections refetch, server tree renders)
- :719-763 button-level keyboard operability (Enter/Space) despite tabindex="-1", and that ArrowUp/Down don't rove focus away from a focused indent/unindent button
- :765-817 promote-to-top-level with no resolvable org fails loudly (banner + no write), never a silently-dead button
- :828-903 the tabindex="-1" pointer-only contract itself, explicitly citing Mihkel's ruling — this is the one pin #252 item 5 says must survive untouched

Zero assertions in this spec touch pixel size, opacity value, color token, or glyph shape/distinguishability — grepped for opacity-30/h-3 w-3/min-h-11/min-w-11/text-ink-2, no hits beyond disabled-boolean checks. So every #252 ask (size, color, opacity/reserved-space, glyph distinction) is free to change without turning any existing test red, EXCEPT the tabindex="-1" assertions at :828-903 — which #252 explicitly says to leave alone.

OVERLAP WITH #253 (same feature, shared code, no expected line collision): both issues act on the identical two <button> elements (+page.svelte:3049-3082), the identical structuralWritePending guard (:1490), and the identical performReparent write seam (:1360-1400). #253 changes what performReparent does (the reparent+renumber write sequence and failure messaging) and does not touch button markup/classes. #252 changes only the button's visual/DOM presentation (size, color, opacity/visibility, glyph choice) and does not touch performReparent, reparentSection, or reorderSections. The two issues cross-reference each other explicitly (#253: "Related: #252"; #252's comment: "#253... is the likelier proximate cause"). Ordering rationale (Gama, both issues agree): fixing #252's cosmetics first would make a control whose underlying write can still half-land easier to find and tap — hence #253 (the write) lands first, #252 (the findability) deliberately last.

Both issues currently carry the `ready` label (checked live) — #252's own body text ("Not ready yet — batched") is stale relative to the label; per this team's ready-label-gate convention the label is authoritative.
